Subject: EU/APAC localization readiness — post-discovery recap & model recommendations

Anna / Carlos — thanks again for the productive discussion earlier. Short recap and our proposed next steps so the pilot can move quickly.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary flows: localized product descriptions (DE/FR/IT/ES), customer-support triage (JA/KO/EN), in-app translation for EU merchants.
- Quality targets: acceptable translation proxy > 0.85, pragmatic pass/fail prompts for legal copy in DE, and p50 token latency target <120ms for chat paths.
- Compliance: EU data residency required; SOC2 evidence & audit logs needed to sign DPA.

Initial model recommendations (shortlist):
- Open-Model-13B (q4f16): cost-efficient baseline that performs well on FR/ES/IT conversational outputs.
- Open-Model-33B (q8): stronger for DE legal/marketing copy where compound noun accuracy and formality matter.
- L2-70B-quant (low-latency variant): target for JA/KO support flows if low-latency generation is prioritized.

Artifacts attached / shared:
- eu_apac_benchmark_summary.pdf (high-level per-locale metrics) — attached
- venturecart_prompt_set_v1.csv (initial prompt templates and anchors) — attached
- Benchmark notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-notebook (reproducible evaluation)

Quality flags we discussed:
- German: model output often drifts informal without explicit style anchors; we recommend anchor examples in prompts and a small in-context tuning set.
- Japanese: honorifics and politeness levels need customer-specific prompt templates; pure zero-shot will fail our 'politeness' gate.
- Thai/Vietnamese: tokenization edge cases require light pre/post-processing in the text normalization step.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Pilot scope + compliance checklist (Ben) — deliver 2026-12-07
2) Sample data intake (VentureCart) — up to 2k rows, CSV with locale tag
3) Preliminary eval run on sample data (Neha) — run after DPA + data delivery (estim 3 business days)
4) Procurement path + DocuSign (Stephanie) — start concurrent with pilot scope

Attachments: venturecart_prompt_set_v1.csv, eu_apac_benchmark_summary.pdf

Open items for you: please confirm the sample dataset format and the primary target locales (we heard DE/FR/JA as top three).

Thanks — happy to schedule a quick follow-up to walk through the benchmark PDF if helpful.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: EU/APAC localization readiness — technical evaluation notes and pilot plan

Anna / Ben — quick technical note while I queue the prelim runs. Summary of how we'll validate and what to expect: 

Evaluation plan (short):
- Smoke run: 200 records per locale to sanity-check prompt templates and tokenization.
- Full prelim: run the 1.5k/300 sample through our eval harness (repro notebook linked in Ben's email).
- Metrics: locale-specific BLEU-like acceptability proxy, exact-match term handling (for legal anchors), and fluency/regression flags (LM-based surprisals).

Prelim results (example expectations based on prior pilots):
- Open-Model-13B (q4): DE acceptability ~0.78-0.83; FR ~0.84-0.88; latency p50 ~110-130ms on our Dedicated profile.
- Open-Model-33B (q8): DE acceptability ~0.86-0.90; better on compound noun handling, p50 ~160-200ms.
- L2-70B-quant: JA politeness pass-rate ~0.80 with prompt anchors; p50 ~95-110ms on the low-latency config (higher GPU footprint).

Practical recommendation: if legal/marketing accuracy in DE is gating, start the legal snippet flow on the 33B (q8) and keep 13B for bulk descriptions. We'll run term-level exact-match checks for your legal anchors and surface any hallucinations as a small 'blocklist' for post-processing.

Data handling / compliance note: to run the harness on your CSV we'll need a signed DPA or temporary data transfer agreement. We can perform the run in a Redwood Dedicated sandbox with EU-region compute to satisfy residency.

Attachments I will include in the run set: eval_harness_runbook.md (short runbook for your engineers), and I'll paste a sample prompt snippet below that we recommend for DE legal copy.

--- sample prompt (DE legal anchor) ---
System: You are a professional legal translator. Maintain formal tone and avoid contractions.
User: Translate the following product description into German legal copy. Preserve technical terms exactly as given.
Example anchor: 
Input: "This product is sold subject to the merchant's standard terms and conditions."
Output (anchor): "Dieses Produkt wird zu den geltenden Allgemeinen Geschäftsbedingungen des Händlers verkauft."
--- end snippet ---

I will start the smoke run today after you confirm dataset headers. Expected turnaround for prelim run: 2 business days after data receipt.

-Neha
